findings.title: traceID silently dropped from "Plugin Request Completed" log lines
findings.body: The previous implementation of logRequest explicitly appended the trace ID to the log params via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). This PR removes that block and instead relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only picks up the contextual attributes stored by ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname). instrumentContext does not add a traceID attribute, so the traceID field is silently lost from these log lines, breaking log-to-trace correlation for plugin requests. This is a behavioral regression in a PR described as a rename-only chore. Fix: add the trace ID back, either by including tracing.TraceIDFromContext in the attributes added by instrumentContext or by continuing to append it in logRequest.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh recorder, making contextual logs invisible to tests
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), a brand-new instance with its own empty Logs fields. Code under test that logs via FromContext — notably the updated LoggerMiddleware, which now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) — will record calls on a throwaway instance, so any test passing a TestLogger and asserting on its InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs counters will observe zero calls and cannot verify log output. The fake should return the receiver itself (or a logger that shares the same recording state) so contextual logging remains observable in tests.

findings.title: Doc comment on Logger.FromContext is a copy of New's and describes the wrong contract
findings.body: The comment on FromContext reads "returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context", which is copied verbatim from New(ctx ...any) and describes New's semantics. FromContext takes a context.Context and returns a logger enriched with the log attributes previously stored in that context (via infra/log.WithContextualAttributes), falling back to the base logger when none are present. As written the comment misleads implementers about what the method must do.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain
findings.body: logRequest no longer derives pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname from the request's PluginContext; those fields only appear in the "Plugin Request Completed" log if NewContextualLoggerMiddleware was registered before NewLoggerMiddleware in the middleware stack. Both constructors are exported and nothing documents or enforces this ordering, so any other wiring that uses NewLoggerMiddleware without the new middleware (tests, alternate client decorators, downstream projects) will silently emit logs missing those fields. Consider documenting the dependency on both constructors or having the logger middleware fall back to the request's PluginContext when no contextual attributes are present.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
findings.body: The PR adds ContextualLoggerMiddleware (instrumentContext plus the four wrapped client methods) but adds no test for it. Nothing verifies that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics attach the endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes to the context, or that the nil DataSourceInstanceSettings and nil User branches behave correctly. Since LoggerMiddleware's log output now depends entirely on these attributes (the inline logParams were removed), a regression here would silently strip fields from plugin request logs without any test failing.
